title: Congressional Marine Liaison (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, OLA
raw_text:
9.     MOS 8018, Congressional Marine Liaison (MGySgt to Sgt) FMOS, OLA

    a. Summary. Congressional Marine Liaisons will serve as an expert on
legislative matters to the Marine Corps. This FMOS is assigned to Marines
that have completed a successful tour as a congressional fellow or served for
a minimum of 18 months within the office of legislative affairs demonstrating
substantial legislative experience. They will be knowledgeable and
considered a subject matter expert with activities related to legislative
affairs. Possessing the FMOS 8018 will assist monitors in slating key
billets requiring Congressional experience. Marines E-5 to E-9 are eligible
to obtain this FMOS.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1)   Must be a U.S. citizen.

        (2) Security requirement: must possess a secret clearance and be
eligible for a top secret clearance.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Successfully complete a tour as a Congressional Fellow (12
months) on Capitol Hill.

        (2) Successfully serve for a minimum of 18 months within the Office
of Legislative Affairs (OLA).

        (3) The certifying authority for MOS 8018 (Free MOSs) is the
Legislative Assistant (LA) to the Commandant of the Marine Corps or Deputy
LA.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Become an expert on legislative matters and advise the
legislative assistant to the commandant on technical and procedural
legislative matters affecting the Marine Corps.

        (2) Plan and coordinate events between the Marine Corps' senior
leadership and congress.

        (3) Support the legislative activities of the Marine Corps senior
leaders including all hearings, briefings, and other engagements.

        (4) Analyze congressional hearing transcripts, the National Defense
Authorization Act and any other pertinent legislation and provide analysis.

        (5) Answer and coordinate responses to questions for the record
(QFRs) from hearings and requests for information (RFIs) from congressional
offices and professional staff members.

        (6) Analyze the proposed legislation from the House and Senate
authorization and appropriation committees in order to inform leadership of
programmatic and budgetary impacts to the Marine Corps.




                                            3-464                   Enclosure (1)
 3149                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



        (7) Support appeals process in response to congressional committees'
proposed legislation.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
